question: What was Noor's latest sleep duration?
headline: Noor's latest sleep duration is 430 minutes with an 'attention' status.

observations.text: The latest evaluation window from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-21 shows a sleep duration of 430 minutes with status 'attention'.
The observed value of 430 minutes is 50 minutes below the personal baseline of 480 minutes.

evidence_context.text: OrbitVitals summary of the NASA web page "Science in Space: Week of Sept. 15, 2023 - Sleep on Station" (section "Science in Space: Week of Sept. 15, 2023 - Sleep on Station"): The Sleep-Long experiment found that scheduled sleep was out of step with the body clock in roughly one of every five sleep episodes on the station. In those episodes crew members slept nearly one hour less and rated their sleep as poorer, and misalignment was more likely in periods of critical operations, for example while a vehicle was docked.

OrbitVitals summary of the NASA web page "Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules" (section "Formal risk description"): This formal risk covers reduced performance and harm to health that can follow from lost sleep, from a body clock out of step with the work schedule (circadian desynchronization) and from excessive workload.

OrbitVitals summary of the NASA web page "Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules" (section "What are the top risks?"): Heavy workloads, irregular light and dark periods and disrupted sleep patterns are among the stressors of spaceflight. Their combined effect on the body can harm health over short and long periods and can put mission success at risk.

interpretations.text: The 'attention' status indicates the algorithm detected a progressive reduction in sleep duration.

uncertainties.text: Some nights in the window have no usable record. The reason is unknown, and a missing night is not evidence of poor or good sleep.
'attention' is produced by screening settings chosen for this demonstration. They are not clinical thresholds, and the screen is not a statistical significance test.
All crew data in this explanation is simulated. It shows how the software behaves, not how a person responds to spaceflight.
The cited summaries of published sources are general context about spaceflight. They do not describe this crew member and do not validate the screening settings.
